newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain, China nears deal on PLA arrival in HK.
newsitem.headline: Britain, China nears deal on PLA arrival in HK.

text.p: China and Britain are close to agreement on the arrival of an advance party of mainland Chinese troops in Hong Kong ahead of the handover, government-funded Radio Television Hong Kong reported on Wednesday.

British Defence Secretary Michael Portillo, who was visiting the colony, was quoted as saying substantial progress on the advance party had been made by the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group, the body handling details of Hong Kong's handover.
Britain hands Hong Kong back to China at midnight on June 30 when the People's Liberation Army (PLA) will replace the British military garrison.

"I'm pleased to say that in the many negotiations ... between the government of Hong Kong and the People's Republic of China, I believe that those negotiations concerning the military handover have been some of the smoothest," Portillo said.
"So although not everything is agreed yet there is substantial agreement and good progress has been made on the outstanding issues," he said.

The radio also reported Portillo as saying that a relatively small number of PLA representatives would be involved, but he declined to comment on recent foreign press reports that the party would be here by April.
A senior Chinese official said late last year the advance party would be about 300 strong and include soldiers and medical and communications staff, who would be housed in closed barracks.
